## Mechanic Signature

| field | design |
| --- | --- |
| wonder_specific_hook | The basilica's authority depends on a named sacred official who can guard relics, regulate pilgrims, account for alms, discipline clergy, and make Rome's apostolic claim legible under the dome. |
| core_interaction_loop | The player opens the threshold dedication, assigns a cardinal, bishop, relic custodian, alms officer, or similar official, resolves the first scandal created by that actor's strengths and weaknesses, and then seals the dedication. |
| player_decision_pattern | Choices trade clerical legitimacy, service competence, estate satisfaction, alms transparency, and pilgrim access rather than accumulating monthly progress. |
| state_feedback_model | The actor slot shows the assigned official and their quality band while the incident log records relic, alms, or pilgrim-access disputes created by that assignment. |
| failure_or_tension_model | A factional or weak official can cause a relic scandal, alms dispute, or access disorder, forcing reassignment or a reduced dedication interpretation. |
| reward_expression | The reward expresses true-faith tolerance and clergy satisfaction as a service network disciplined by a credible official. |
| reuse_risk_mitigation | This assignment belongs to Saint Peter's because the apostolic tomb, Rome, relic custody, alms, pilgrim thresholds, and clerical obligations converge in one sacred office. |

### Risk Branches

| --- | --- | --- |

| alms_dispute | Alms officers and pilgrims accuse the basilica of buying splendor with poor relief. | Redirect one-time reward into alms or take an incident penalty before final dedication. |
| factional_official | A strong candidate belongs to a faction that wants patronage control over chapels or offerings. | Keep the candidate for stronger service but accept estate tension, or retry with a weaker neutral official. |
